ai.description: The Olive Dasia (Scincidae) reaches 20 cm. It is olive-brown with a pale, speckled underside and a distinct dark lateral stripe. It features a smooth, iridescent body and a blunt, rounded snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Dasia olivacea* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark-edged pale spots on the back and a lack of the prominent longitudinal stripes found on other Indian skinks.
ai.habitat: *Dasia olivacea* inhabits tropical evergreen and moist deciduous forests in the Indian subcontinent, typically residing in tree canopies at low to moderate altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Olive Dasia is primarily arboreal and diurnal, often seen foraging for insects and small invertebrates among the high canopy and tree trunks of tropical forests.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dasia olivacea* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–8 eggs. In India, breeding typically occurs during the warmer months, often peaking between April and June.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Dasia olivacea* is found in the Western Ghats of India, primarily in moist deciduous and evergreen forests at elevations ranging from sea level to 1,000 meters.
